== Biography ==
Samuel was born in 1814. He passed away in 1906.

== Research Notes ==
=== Peoria family and paternal inference — 23 October 2026 ===

A published transcription of the August 1904 obituaries of [[Glasgow-17|Stewart Glasgow]] names his surviving brother Samuel Steel Glasgow in his 90th year. Samuel's retained birth of 12 September 1814 fits that wording, and the Adams County, Ohio–Peoria family context matches.<ref name="StewartObituary1904">''Peoria Star'', 24 August 1904, abridged obituary of Stewart Glasgow; and ''Monmouth Review'', 24 August 1904, obituary attributed to the ''Peoria Herald Transcript'', transcribed in [https://www.werelate.org/wiki/Person:Stewart_Glasgow_(1) WeRelate, Stewart Glasgow, Biography], inspected 23 October 2026. Published transcription only; original newspaper images not inspected. The accounts may derive from one report.</ref>

[[Glasgow-8|Robert Barclay Glasgow]] is confidently inferred as Samuel's father, assessed at 92%. This is a subjective assessment of the complete Samuel/father pair, increasing the earlier 58% possible assessment. The sibling evidence combines with Stewart's separately assessed 94% father relationship: the 1925 recollection names [[Glasgow-8|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Finley-134|Rosanna Finley]] as parents of [[Glasgow-16|Finley]] and [[Glasgow-17|Stuart]], while the Peoria residence, first wife [[Askren-120|Elizabeth Askren]] and son [[Glasgow-1923|Huston]] connect that Stuart to Stewart's 1880 family sketch.<ref>Josiah V. Thompson, ''Family Record'', vol. 15, p. 101, household interview, 24 October 1925; [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=659 Uniontown Public Library transcription, PDF p. 659]. Modern transcription of retrospective family recollection, not a manuscript facsimile.</ref><ref>Josiah V. Thompson, ''Family Record'', vol. 15, pp. 98–99, interview, 24 October 1925; [https://uniontownlib.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/JV_Thompson_Journals_Vo13_thru19.pdf#page=658 Uniontown Public Library transcription, PDF p. 658]. Names Stuart in Peoria and his first wife Elizabeth Askain [transcriber's best guess]. The recollection's recent-death estimate and later-wife account have discrepancies.</ref><ref>''The History of Peoria County, Illinois'' (Chicago: Johnson &amp; Company, 1880), pp. 791–792, Stewart Glasgow sketch; [https://archive.org/details/historyofpeoriac00john/page/791/mode/1up Internet Archive]. Names first wife Elizabeth Askren and son Huston, but does not itself name Stewart's parents. Its birth-day and Huston-age details differ from other held accounts.</ref>

The obituary supplies a sibling relationship, not a literal statement of Samuel's father. The paternal conclusion is an inference from that relationship and Stewart's established paternal identity, with compatible chronology and no known concrete conflicting parentage. The newspaper originals remain uninspected, and the retrospective interviews may share family tradition. Samuel's mother is assessed separately; this review makes no maternal change.

The dated 22 October assessment below is superseded by this combined evidence. Inspecting the original newspaper pages and Samuel's own parent-bearing records remains useful.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-8]] is assessed at 58% (possible). The inherited descendant family places Samuel Steele Glasgow, born 1814 in Adams County, under Robert Barclay and Rosanna Finley. Robert’s 1783 generation and established Ohio family fit a31-year fatherhood. The held 1880/1900 censuses identify Samuel’s later life, but do not name his parents.

Possible58%; the specific existing household is preferred, with no independently inspected father clause or fabricated maternal naming argument.

Next useful test: Check the Faris descendant entry, family papers or Samuel’s obituary for parent names.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-9 WikiTree profile export for Glasgow-9]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.
